LESSON: FICTION AND NON- FICTION 4.3.1 FICTION: THE PLAY FROM KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Fiction and Non- fiction 4.3.1 Fiction: The Play from Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non- fiction 4.3.1 Fiction: The Play from Kenya, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is the play important in studying literature?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. analyse the structure of a

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- fiction 4.3.1 Fiction: The Play from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. analyse the structure of a

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online or offline for the meaning of a play. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non- fiction 4.3.1 Fiction: The Play from Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: This is enhanced as the learner searches independently on the structure of a play and summarises the

findings on a chart.

● Citizenship: This is enhanced as learner appreciates peers input in group tasks when teaming up with peers to conduct a

reading session on plays from Kenya and make reviews.

Values:
● Love: This is enhanced as the learner participates in group activities and shares responses with peers.

● Respect: This is nurtured as the learner appreciates others contributions during discussions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social economic issues: This is propagated as the learner tackles issues on environmental education and climate change in a

play.
